title: 1990 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: A straight concrete sidewalk is to be \(3\) feet wide, \(60\) feet long, and \(3\) inches thick. How many cubic yards of concrete must a contractor order for the sidewalk if concrete must be ordered in a whole number of cubic yards?

solutions.text:
The thickness is \(3\) inches \(= \dfrac14\) foot, so the volume is \(3 \cdot 60 \cdot \dfrac14 = 45\) cubic feet.

Since \(1\) cubic yard \(= 27\) cubic feet, this is \(\dfrac{45}{27} = 1\dfrac23\) cubic yards. Rounding up to a whole number, the contractor must order \(2\) cubic yards.

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: First convert \(3\) inches to feet: \(3 \text{ in} = \dfrac14 \text{ ft}\)
Find the volume in cubic feet, then divide by \(27\) since \(1\) cubic yard \(= 27\) cubic feet
